extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers and experimentalists (early-modern practitioners of natural philosophy, alchemists, and makers of experiments)
extracted.subtask_description: Methodological guidance for investigating natural bodies: classification of motions, rules for determining predominance, and seven principal methods by which man acts on nature (exclusion, compression, heat/cold, continuance, direction, harmony, alternation). Includes experimental suggestions and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifteenth motion — transmission or of passage
rubrics_metrics.description: The powers of bodies are more or less impeded or advanced by the medium; one medium is adapted to light, another to sound, another to heat and cold, another to magnetic action, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying or experimenting with interactions, account for the medium's selective adaptation to different actions; consider how a medium transmits or impedes specific powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixteenth motion — the royal or political motion
rubrics_metrics.description: A predominant and governing part of any body checks, subdues, reduces, and regulates the others, forcing them to unite, separate, stand still, move, or assume a certain position — a dominion or civil government of parts over subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for predominance in composite bodies (e.g., spirits in animals temper other motions; in denser bodies grosser parts may predominate). Consider whether a transformation requires throwing off the governing part or otherwise overcoming its 'yoke.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventeenth motion — spontaneous motion of revolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies in a favorable situation pursue their peculiar nature, moving in eternal circles, resting if they abhor motion, or moving in straight lines to unite with congenial natures; this motion admits nine differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing revolution, examine nine differences: (1) the centre about which bodies move; (2) the poles of motion; (3) the circumference/orbit relative distance; (4) velocity; (5) direction (east→west or reverse); (6) deviation from perfect circle by spirals at varying distances from centre; (7) deviation by spirals at varying distances from poles; (8) distance between spirals; (9) variation of movable poles (affecting circular revolution). Apply these distinctions to celestial/terrestrial debates and to rotating projectiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighteenth motion — trepidation
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion of (as it were) eternal captivity: bodies placed in a mean state (neither properly placed nor wholly displaced) constantly tremble and are restless — e.g., heart and pulse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify trepidation in systems that are 'in a mean state'; treat such restless tendency as a distinct species when investigating natural tendencies and rhythms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nineteenth motion — repose or abhorrence of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendency to rest: dense bodies abhor motion and tend to recover a former state; extremes move toward the middle (earth by its weight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for tendencies toward rest and the active manner in which bodies attempt to regain rest after being moved; do not treat rest as mere absence of motion but as an effective tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify motions by invincibility, reach, immediacy, and mutual direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Some motions are quite invincible; others more powerful than others. Motions direct and are directed by each other according to their strength, quantity, excitement, emission, or assistance/impediments they meet with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating competing powers, compare their strength, range, immediacy, and interactions; collect 'wrestling instances' showing predominance (e.g., magnets lifting iron, levers vs weight, leather vs tension, chinks for flowing water, gunpowder vs confinement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the nature and manner of yielding in conflicts of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether yielding motions completely cease or exert themselves invisibly (apparent rest vs real rest), as in equilibrium or absolute predominance; check for continued but unseen effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments to reveal latent motion in apparently yielded systems (e.g., bound man struggling, musket-ball striking point-blank vs upward to detect concurrence of motions). Observe concurrence rather than only visible conflict outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect rules of predominance
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate general rules governing which motion prevails: e.g., the more general the desired advantage, the stronger the motion; motion of connection (universal intercourse) may be more powerful than gravity (intercourse of dense bodies only); public good tends to prevail over private good except in small quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather instances that reveal systematic rules of predominance and apply these inferentially to new cases; use analogies between natural and civil predominance where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — suggesting instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that suggest or point out what is advantageous to mankind; bare power and knowledge exalt rather than enrich human nature, so select from the general store those things most useful to mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When organizing knowledge, give priority to instances that suggest practical advantage; reserve space for the 'human or optative chart' to translate science into beneficial applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — generally useful instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that recur across points and spare labor and new trials; these concern instruments and contrivances and should be described in histories of each art and in practical application sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect broadly useful examples and contrivances that apply across multiple problems; catalogue them to reduce redundant experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 1 — exclusion of all that impedes and disturbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude common air and rays of heavenly bodies and other disturbances to preserve or control bodies; e.g., vessel thickness, hermetical closing, lutum sapientiæ, oil on wine, powders, wax, honey, pitch, immersion in quicksilver, grottoes/subterranean storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sealing, immersion, burial, and protective constructions to prevent admission of external agents and loss of internal 'spirits'. Consider devices (e.g., hollow metal tub for divers) and storage practices (submerging, subterranean granaries) to shield specimens during experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 2 — compression, extension, agitation, and the like
rubrics_metrics.description: Violent compression and similar operations can produce locomotion or destroy organic qualities; they often produce transient states that tend to return to former habit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment whether condensations effected by violence can be made permanent via perseverance or harmonies (e.g., compressing homogeneous bodies like air or water, sealing glass eggs after exhausting air, leaving compressed bodies for days). If simple perseverance fails, combine with other methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 3 — heat and cold
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat is abundant to man but cold scarce; seek natural and artificial sources of cold and study condensations effected by cold and substitutes that mimic cold's operation. Investigate every kind and degree of heat (sun rays, lightning, furnaces, moist heats, animal heat, dry heats) and their modes (direct, reflected, refracted, condensed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for cold in caverns, wells, quicksilver immersion, burial; test substitutes for cold (condensation by compression, escape of finer parts, cohesion of solid homogeneous parts, harmony). Study effects of gradual, periodic, and properly spaced approaches/withdrawals of heat; avoid assuming equable heat suffices for natural processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 4 — continuance (detention in a suitable place)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandon a body to itself for observable time, guarded from external force, to let internal motions manifest (continuance is steward of nature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use continuance for delicate incorporations and mixtures that fire cannot produce (e.g., wine clarification, slow natural conformations). Note vessel state: open for separation, hermetically sealed for mixtures, partly closed for putrefaction. Collect numerous instances of temporal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 5 — checking or directing motion (direction of motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrest, repel, allow, or direct original motions via figure and position of vessels and internal bodies (e.g., upright cone condenses vapor in alembics; inverted cones refine sugar; strainers; pebbles collect mud; egg white refines syrups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design forms (curved, alternately contracted/dilated) and internal obstacles to direct constituent motions; apply to casting, modelling, refining and separating operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 6 — peculiar harmonies and aversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Occult sympathies and antipathies (harmony/aversion) arise from correspondence of form or substance; broader harmonies include correspondences among sulphur, mercury, flame, water, air, etc.; grafting and soil compatibility are instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate correspondences of conformation and of supporting media (climate, soil, depth for metals and gems, manure types for plants). Seek natural harmonies but postpone until forms and simple conformations are better known; record grafting and compatibility instances for practical horticulture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 7 — seasonable and proper alternation, series, and succession
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper alternation and succession of methods (and their timing) is a principal way man acts on nature and often necessary for producing desired effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine methods in timely sequences (e.g., gradual approach/withdrawal of heat, alternating exposures) to mimic natural processes; design experiments with intervals and periodicity rather than continuous violent application.
